To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the land-use changes have altered the hydroclimate of central Taiwan in a manner that is strongly associated with local topography and the prevailing wind.
land use and cover change in central Taiwan since the 1995 has led to increased urban heat island and intensified precipitation over the urban and built-up areas, especially during rainy periods.
the LUCC has increased the urban heat island and the JA rainfall in the downwind area of central Taiwan.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the hydroclimatology in response to the LUCC and its impacts on the rainfall over central Taiwan.
the impacts of LUCC on the local climate in central Taiwan.
the impacts of the land use/cover on the regional precipitation, which has not been addressed in the previous studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
LUCC has intensified the hydroclimatology of central Taiwan.
LUCC in central Taiwan has intensified the JA rainfall, particularly for the downwind areas.
LUCC has altered the local and regional climate of central Taiwan, and the WRF modeling is a viable tool for the study of LUCC impacts on the climate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the LUCC has altered the local hydroclimatology in central Taiwan.
the LUCC in the central Taiwan has induced a local and regional hydroclimate response in terms of the sensible heat fluxes, 2 m temperature and humidity, and precipitation.
LUCC has intensified the local rainfall in the study region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LUCC has altered the local and regional climate in central Taiwan.
the LUCC in central Taiwan is a significant contributor to the recent change in rainfall, which has been attributed to climate change.
the LUCC is a significant factor in modulating the JA rainfall in central Taiwan, which should be accounted for in hydroclimate studies in the region.
